title: ～ないで — “without doing ～”
summary: Says that you do one thing without doing another. It is the nai-form of a verb plus で, in the pattern 〜しないで〜する.

body.p: 朝ご飯を食べないで学校へ行きました means going to school without having breakfast. The first action is skipped, and the second happens.
In writing you can also say 食べずに with the same meaning.
At the end of a sentence, ないで is also a casual request (行かないで).

examples.ja: 朝（あさ）ご飯（はん）を食（た）べないで学校（がっこう）へ行（い）きました。
examples.romaji: Asagohan o tabenaide gakkō e ikimashita.
examples.tr: I went to school without eating breakfast.

examples.ja: 電気（でんき）を消（け）さないで寝（ね）ました。
examples.tr: I went to sleep without turning off the light.

examples.ja: 傘（かさ）を持（も）たないで出（で）かけました。
examples.tr: I went out without taking an umbrella.

pitfalls: Do not confuse it with なくて, which gives a cause (食べなくて困った).
The form of する is しないで.
